Table 16: Implicit radiologist baseline on LGE and T2 image understanding. F1 (%) under random selection at K ∈ {8, 32, 128}. K=32 and K=128 typically exceed the per-study slice count for LGE and T2, so the model has access to at least as much visual evidence as the reporting radiologist. Because ground-truth labels are derived from radiologist-finalized reports, a radiologist achieves 100% F1 by construction; the gap to 100% is therefore an information-matched comparison.

Table 13: Comparison with representative medical LLM/MLLM benchmarks. Data: input modality and dimensionality. Source: Pub. (public repositories), Priv. (private hospital archives). Scale: number of evaluation items (QA pairs, reports, or rationales). Integration: the level of multisource information a task requires the model to jointly reason over—e.g., multiple views, imaging sequences, or temporal frames of the same patient. Perception: image-level understanding tasks (VQA, modality/anatomy recognition). Reporting: free-form long report or rationale generation. Slice Protocol: standardized slice-selection protocol that disentangles input-construction effects from intrinsic competence.

Table 12: Comparison with representative cardiac MRI datasets. Each dataset is characterized by six binary attributes and two quantitative attributes. The binary attributes are: Multi-Seq. – provides more than one MRI sequence; Multi-View – provides multiple acquisition views (e.g., short-axis, 2-/3-/4- chamber long-axis); Reports – provides paired radiology reports; Diagnosis – provides patient-level diagnostic labels; Temporal – provides time-resolved imaging across the cardiac cycle (e.g., cine sequences or first-pass perfusion dynamics) rather than only static snapshots. Sequences lists the MRI sequences included, and Scale reports the number of unique patients and the total number of imaging volumes. A red ✓ indicates the attribute is supported; ✗ indicates it is not.
